question.text: Vikram, a Resident Indian, receives IDCW of Rs.12,000 from an equity mutual fund during the financial year. He has not submitted his PAN to the fund house. What is the TDS rate applicable?

answer.text: Nil, as IDCW up to Rs.5,000 is exempt

explanation.text: The Logic: Where PAN is not available or has not been submitted by the unit holder, TDS on IDCW is deducted at 20% instead of the normal 10% applicable to resident investors with PAN. The Trap: The 10% rate (and the related Rs.5,000-per-year threshold) is for residents who have submitted their PAN. Without PAN the rate doubles to 20%. Note: Always ensure PAN is recorded in the folio so the lower 10% TDS rate applies.
